Installation

Install from source with Bun. You need Bun plus a reachable browser: an agent-browser daemon (the installer sets one up), any Chrome with a debug port, or a remote CDP endpoint your driver skill knows.

Prerequisites

  • Bun — the toolchain. Get it at bun.sh.
  • agent-browser — the browser the engine connects to: npm i -g agent-browser, then agent-browser install (downloads Chromium). Any CDP endpoint works, but this is the zero-setup path the installer uses.
  • No account, no registry service, nothing hosted.

Install from source

git clone <repo> agent-webmcp && cd agent-webmcpbun installbun run gate        # deterministic checks — green or stopbun run compile     # dist/agent-webmcp, standalone binary
bash

Release binaries (per-OS, no registry) attach to GitHub releases from 1.0 on — beta installs are source-only (see Staying current above). Until then, the binary you just compiled is the install: put dist/agent-webmcp on your PATH.

export PATH="$PWD/dist:$PATH"agent-webmcp --version   # expect 0.1.0-beta.x
bash

Staying current (beta)

Beta means breaking changes can ship in any release — each one is listed at the top of its changelog entry, with no migration scripts until 1.0. To update a source install in place (pull, gate, compile, reinstall, with a .prev backup of your old binary):

agent-webmcp upgrade --yes                 # uses your checkout (walks up to .git)agent-webmcp upgrade --repo ~/agent-webmcp --yes
bash

No checkout on this machine (binary-only install)? Re-run the installer instead:

curl -fsSL https://agent-webmcp.vercel.app/install.sh | bash
bash

Per-release binaries attach to GitHub releases from 1.0 on; until then source builds plus upgrade are the distribution.

Verify the install

agent-webmcp doctor      # environment reportagent-webmcp mcp list    # the 9 served tools
bash

doctor prints a JSON environment report (Bun version, platform, Effect version, browser reachability, resolved config). If open later fails with no browser reachable, start an agent-browser daemon or pass --cdp (your driver skill knows the endpoint).

Add it as an MCP server

{  "mcp": {    "agent-webmcp": {      "command": ["agent-webmcp", "mcp", "serve"]    }  }}
json

Pin the registry root in the server entry so every spawned server resolves identically (some harnesses spawn per-call servers with varying working directories):

{  "mcp": {    "agent-webmcp": {      "command": [        "agent-webmcp",        "mcp",        "serve",        "--registry",        "/abs/path/.agent-webmcp/registry"      ]    }  }}
json

Then read the version-matched contract with agent-webmcp skill show. See Commands for serve flags and root pinning.
